prevalenceNote: Each row gives the share of people of an age band who already have the condition, at the band's middle age. Between middles the share slides in a straight line; below the first middle it slides to zero at the band's start, and above the last it holds. A band's share is the source's figure, not a modeled one.

mortalityWeight.note: Calibrated (Ruling 39) so births before 28 weeks carry the first year's strain; a condition of birth takes no severity grade or age factor.

prevalence.note: Children held at these ages only. ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: England counts 66 per 10,000 children and young people with a life-limiting or life-threatening condition (Fraser et al., Palliative Medicine 2021); no US count is read yet. The share here is the calibrated one (Ruling 39), below that count, because most such children live many years.

mortalityWeight.note: Calibrated (Ruling 39) against the table's death rate at ages 1 to 14; carries no severity grade or age factor.

onsetCauses.note: Conditions that begin during life (Ruling 38, step 2): each condition's strain grows from the life table's age hazard times the condition's onset scale, times these recorded causes, and the condition begins when it crosses the same fixed threshold as mortality strain. Only causes the world records today are read; smoking and occupation are not recorded and are missing links. An infant row has no onset scale: it is a condition of birth, not one that begins later.
missingLinks: smoking: no person record says whether someone smokes; it drives heart disease, cancer, COPD and stroke
occupation exposure: employment records name the job, but no record says what the work exposes a person to

belowPovertyLine.note: Read from the person's latest coverage record: household income against the federal poverty line.

uncovered.note: Read from the person's latest coverage record saying not covered.

severityGrades.note: Calibrated (Ruling 39) against the SSA 2023 table, not yet read from a source. A person holding a condition holds it at one grade, chosen once when the condition is recorded, among these shares. Real grades exist for each condition (cancer stage at diagnosis, heart failure class, COPD GOLD stage); research question chronic-condition-severity-shares.

ageFactor.note: Calibrated (Ruling 39). A condition recorded young weighs more: its weight is multiplied by 1 + (youngFactor - 1) / (1 + e^((age - turnAge) / widthYears)), read once at the age it is recorded. Cohort studies find chronic-condition hazard ratios fall with age; the size here also stands in for the external causes of death at working ages that no producer writes yet.

baseRateScale.note: Calibrated (Ruling 39). The life table's hazard counts against the strain threshold at this scale, so a person whose records multiply nothing lives past the table's median: the table's average includes the people with conditions. Checked on totals only, by the synthetic-cohort test.
